Robinhood Chain is getting close to $1B in TVL, and @virtuals_io had already reported 5.6K+ AI agent launches there in August.

That got me looking a bit closer at the AI infrastructure being built on Robinhood.

A few projects caught my eye:

→ @usepaygent lets you give an existing agent a crypto-funded virtual card through MCP, which connects it to external tools.

Say you ask an agent to build a website for a client. You could give it a budget to buy the domain and pay for hosting as part of the job.

→ @helloSQD makes blockchain data available to agents through MCP. So an agent researching activity on Robinhood Chain could pull up transfers and swaps to help it understand what’s happening.

→ @ClawBankHQ is building financial + legal infrastructure for agents: bank accounts, crypto wallets, company formation, contracts, and payment rails, all accessible through MCP/API.

An agent researching activity on Robinhood Chain could pull transfers, swaps, and other onchain data to understand what is actually happening.

Most of this infrastructure is still aimed at devs and companies, but the direction is becoming pretty clear.

@RobinhoodCrypto is pushing deeper into agentic trading and payments, while projects around it are building the accounts, data, and transaction rails agents need to operate.

The next question is whether that narrative can attract real liquidity and users.

@usepaygent’s TGE is happening on September 8, which should be an interesting first test. As a Paygent supporter, I'll definitely be watching it.

A few weeks ago, it felt like everyone on the timeline thought crypto was dead.

So I wanted to see how much money VCs were actually putting into crypto this year compared to previous cycles. It’s an interesting leading indicator.

Well, crypto investment hit $13.3B in the first half of 2026, including acquisitions. 

2024 took 12 months to hit roughly that number…2026 did it in six.

That matters because investors aren't putting up that kind of money unless they expect a decent ROI. They can be wrong, but billions still being deployed is a useful counterpoint to the idea that crypto is dead.

There's something different happening compared to past cycles:

• Deals per month are down 56% from 2022
• Seed rounds per month are down roughly 77%

But the reported average deal size went from $11.7M in 2024 to $47.4M in H1 2026.

Basically, no more spraying and praying. They're writing huge checks to a handful of proven companies (Kalshi, Polymarket, stablecoin rails) and being much more selective about everything else.

The upside to this is we're seeing a new generation of dApps with no VC money behind them.

That means no VC allocations waiting to unlock, or VC funds waiting to dump on you at TGE. 

This is much healthier compared to what we had in the past.

🚨 BREAKING NEWS: HAPAG-LLOYD AND FIMI ARE PUSHING HARD FOR APPROVAL OF THE $ZIM DEAL

A new article reports that they received another 30 days to improve the offer and address the Israeli government’s concerns. The revised structure would give Israel greater control over $ZIM Israel, direct access to 16 new ships, and stronger protection of strategic shipping routes.

https://t.co/cEdugahZY3

OUR TAKE:

The stated buyout price is $35 per share, valuing $ZIM at approximately $4.2 billion. However, once you include employee compensation, the assets and part of the business being transferred to FIMI, and other expenses, Hapag-Lloyd is effectively paying around $45 per share. This means its models likely valued $ZIM at at least $60 per share when they made the offer.

And that valuation was calculated before the “golden swan” event we are now witnessing in shipping rates, which is nothing short of historic and re rating the entire industry. 

Why would Hapag-Lloyd pay so much? Because it understands that $ZIM is worth much more.

Take a pen and paper and add up all of $ZIM’s assets, cash, vessels, and long-term charter contracts. You can easily reach a sum-of-the-parts valuation of more than $100 per share.

But even that calculation understates the real value because many of these assets cannot simply be bought today, regardless of how much money you have. The average delivery time for a new container ship is more than three years, while many large LNG dual-fuel ships ordered today will not be delivered until 2029 or 2030.

Recreating $ZIM’s fleet, contracts, routes, and operating network would take years. That scarcity makes the whole company worth considerably more than the simple sum of its parts.

The original $35 bid was made when shipping rates were far lower. It is like bidding for an oil company when oil is at $60, while oil is now trading at $90.

At current rates, $ZIM will have more than $30 per share in cash by year-end, more than its entire current public market value ($28.5).

With aggressive buybacks and dividends, it is easy to see $ZIM doubling from here within the next few years while continuing to offer one of the highest dividend yields in the market.

for the newly minted fomo users who are realising that memes have no moat beyond attention and are dipping their toes into fundamentals, here's a simple checklist of what differentiates tokens

1. Who they are, background, founding team, what’s your edge in this space? - ultimately this space is all founder quality, that's what drives 100x outcomes. Crypto's bar is so low that the difference b/w an A tier and B tier operator is 100s of m in mc; also guarantees you won't get rug if they're serious operators

2. Value accrual - What is the token, what is it being used for and how does it accrue value to long term investors

Moat 2 is how the token accrues value. You may think all tokens are the same but they're not. Hyperliquid is an extreme example and not really feasible for an example tbh. Too many people use HYPE and say people should do that. They shouldn't. But they should have some sort of focus for the token, and above all else, the token cannot have some sort of bundle (whether snipers, investors, VC unlocks) dumping millions in MC into market

3. Product - GTM / Distribution / Catalysts / Thematic / Growth; Why does the product have PMF & how do you differentiate from competitors ; Is this actually a problem, and how do you solve it?

Firstly high growth themes are real; Perps / launchpads are more "sexy" than say, bridges or yield farms. Generally the idea also has to have some sort of huge untapped blue ocean (e.g Digital Collectibles, or AI) and a product that has genuine usage and traction (the fabled PMF!)

4. Others
- Biz / monetization models - less important for memes, and less impt in certain market conditions. will be important eventually 
- Runway, profitability, raising, financial metrics - hard to get unless you have founder access

So, how much does it cost? Assuming Jensen means 100k GPUs, I looked up public rental prices for GB300 NVL72 and Verda lists $8.62 per GPU per hour.

That’s $862,000 an hour. $20.7 million a day. $620.6 million a month. So suppose the pre-training run is 3 months, running 24/7: $1.86 BILLION!! 

And then, obviously, they still need to do a lot of post-training. Obviously, you cannot just add 100,000 GPUs to your cart and click checkout. And yes, you probably negotiate a much better price when buying in bulk so this is a public list price ballpark, not the actual bill.

But it gives you a sense of the scale. A billion dollar training run, plus all the experiments it took to get there, and then a whole lot more compute for post-training.
